title: Geo & Tier Failover Composer — interactive Console policy editor with preview and validator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an interactive policy composer inside the Redwood Console that lets customers author routing policies combining region preferences, tier routing priorities (hosted/dedicated/private) and explicit fallback model variants. The UI must provide: 1) a visual editor for rule composition (drag-to-order region/tier chains), 2) a validation pass that surfaces incompatible model variants or region constraints, and 3) a live preview/simulator that shows route selection outcomes for sample request patterns. Deliver an MVP that covers common flows and a roadmap for advanced semantics (intent-aware routing, weighted distributions, variable latency thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Editor: users can create a policy composed of ordered rules: region -> tier -> model_variant with a human-readable breadcrumb for each rule.
Validation: the console flags invalid combinations (e.g., model_variant not available in region, tier mismatch) with actionable fixes and links to model catalog docs.
Preview: simulator runs 3 sample scenarios (low latency region, cost-first fallback, region outage) and shows deterministic route decisions with reasons per request.
Export & API: policy can be saved and exposed to policy engine via API (policy ID returned), and a change creates a changelog entry visible in the Console.
Telemetry: when toggled, the preview emits a synthetic trace to the routing dashboard and shows expected token-cost delta estimates.
Rollout: feature is gated behind feature-flag console.routing-composer and can be canaried to 5% of orgs for 2 weeks prior to full release.
comments: 2026-01-10 Maya Chen: Initial proposal drafted after customer call (ACME Health). Customers asked for region-first policies that fall back to cheaper tiers automatically when capacity is constrained.
2026-01-15 Design review (Anika Patel): Proposed wireframes uploaded to Figma; suggested stronger affordances for 'why this route' explanations. Link added to links field.

2026-01-21 ENG sync (Diego Ramos): Runtime needs two API endpoints: policy validation and a deterministic simulator. ENG will own validation endpoint (ENG-21011) and simulator (ENG-21345) as dependencies.
2026-01-28 PM decision: Split MVP. Phase 1 = visual composer + validation + basic preview. Phase 2 = probability weighting, intent routing, and bulk import of legacy policies.
2026-02-02 Liam O'Connor: UX polish done for rule list, added inline 'fix' actions for validation failures. Working with SRE to add synthetic trace ingestion for preview telemetry.
qa_checks: Create policies that reference a model_variant which is not available in the chosen region and confirm validation error with suggested actions.
Simulate region outage in preview and verify fallback to next tier/model_variant and display of rationale.
Verify save/export creates policy ID and appears in policy list and audit log with correct metadata.
Confirm feature flag gating behavior and canary rollout control, including rollback path.
rollout_notes: Phase 1: enable behind feature flag for 5% of orgs for two weeks. Monitor routing decisions and cost delta via preview telemetry dashboard.
Phase 2: enable for all orgs and add bulk import; run a 48-hour smoke test to ensure validation endpoint handles production traffic.
Fallback plan: if policy validation latency > 200ms, disable live validation and fall back to server-side batch validation to avoid blocking saves.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: inline validation provides immediate feedback but increases latency for saves; we will implement optimistic local validation with server-side authoritative check.
Design decision: use a single ordered rule list (region first) for MVP rather than a full policy DSL — simplifies UX and reduces support surface.
Open question: how to expose cost estimates when model pricing differs by region/tier. Product to follow up with pricing/finance to supply per-variant cost profiles.
Related customer asks: ACME Health wants strict region pinning for compliance; include 'hard pin' toggle that blocks fallbacks for high-compliance policies.
